purpose: Does the simulated 2D ridge over- or under-estimate the field of a compact 3D particle carrying the same eigenstrain?

md_ridge_measurement_MPa.cell: Al matrix + Fe4Al13 ridge, 66698 atoms, CG minimisation only, no dislocations, no solutes
md_ridge_measurement_MPa.label: stage G13 perturbation pair, unified 91,428-atom cell, eigenstrain on the ridge only, built from the v3-relaxed control, CG to a force two-norm of 0.02; inclusion tethered (spring/self 20 eV/A^2); profile to 20 A below the free surface

at_measured_FeAl_magnetostriction.note: what the same sphere would carry if its strain were the largest magnetostriction reported for bulk Fe-Al alloys (Hall 1959; Bormio-Nunes 2012), i.e. 20-100 times less than 0.194 %

verdict: At identical eigenstrain the compact 3D inclusion carries an interior max-RSS of 41.5 MPa against 39.0 MPa for the infinite cylinder, a ratio of 1.06. The exterior field of the sphere falls to 11.34 MPa at r = 1.5a and 1.43 MPa at r = 3a. The MD ridge cell (docs/reports/stageG10_field_profile.json) gives a peak max-RSS of 5.0 MPa at r = 50 A from the interface plane, and 15.4 MPa within 10 A of the ridge axis. At the largest magnetostriction measured for bulk Fe-Al alloys (1e-4) the same sphere would carry 2.14 MPa.
